process.top_down: Top Down Analysis: start from a main (higher) timeframe, zoom into lower timeframes to identify key levels, and go to the lowest timeframes for execution (trader, 2026-09-26). More examples to come.

terminology.CHoCH: Change of character. Bullish CHoCH requires a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
terminology.extreme demand level: The red box: the full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest.
terminology.extreme supply level: Mirror of extreme demand, at the higher high.
terminology.invalidation %: Distance from entry to stop, in percent.
terminology.lower low: A candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). Vice versa for a higher high.
terminology.reclaim: Price back above a swept level, holding it as support; secondary entry.
terminology.confluences: Liquidity sweep; strong bullish momentum + volume; inducement; potential resistance level.
terminology.Top Down Analysis: Main timeframe first, then lower timeframes for key levels, then the lowest timeframes for execution.
terminology.key level: Support/resistance drawn from a wick; valid after multiple reactions.
terminology.deviation: Price moves through a level and fails to hold: a fakeout.
terminology.retest: Price returns to a broken level and tests it from the other side.
terminology.reclaim-retest-accept: Long sequence: level reclaimed, retested from above, and held.

sources.risk.max_risk_per_trade_pct: Inferred from 'always 1%': fixed risk means 1% is also the ceiling. Confirm.
sources.leverage.margin_mode: Trader: 'which means I use an isolated margin', 2026-09-26
sources.risk.min_rr: Trader: 'I could enter a trade with 1:2,5RR as well', 2026-09-26

choch.label: CHoCH (change of character)
choch.definition: Bullish CHoCH requires a candle CLOSE above the last lower high; a wick through does not count.

extreme_demand.label: Extreme demand level
extreme_demand.definition: The red box: the full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest (trader, 2026-09-26).

reclaim.label: Reclaim (support reclaim)
reclaim.definition: Price closes back above a level it swept (in T-0001 the former inducement / equal lows) and holds it as support. Used as a secondary entry.

extreme_supply.label: Extreme supply level
extreme_supply.definition: Mirror of extreme demand: the full wick-to-wick range of the high-volume candle at the higher high.

key_level.label: Key level (S/R)
key_level.definition: Support/resistance level drawn from a wick. It is valid once price has reacted to it multiple times (trader, T-0003).

deviation.label: Deviation (fakeout)
deviation.definition: Price moves through a level and fails to hold beyond it (trader's words: 'deviation/fakeout').

retest.label: Retest
retest.definition: Price returns to a level it just broke or lost and tests it from the other side.

premature_exit.label: Exited before the plan's exit criteria

cut_winner_early.label: Cut winner / took profit too early

A.label: Good loss
A.meaning: Valid setup, controlled risk, plan followed; the trade simply failed.
A.lesson: Keep the process. Do not change the strategy because of one normal loss.

B.label: Strategy failure
B.meaning: Setup looked valid but the strategy may underperform in these conditions.
B.lesson: Investigate the conditions under which the strategy fails.

C.label: Execution error
C.meaning: Strategy valid, execution deviated from the plan.
C.lesson: Fix execution rather than the strategy.

D.label: Invalid setup
D.meaning: The trade should never have been taken.

E.label: Information deficiency
E.meaning: Reasonable decision on available information; later information invalidated the thesis.
E.lesson: Only add a rule if the missing information was knowable and recurs. Do not overfit one loss.

meta.name: Key level S/R: reclaim-retest-accept / deviation-retest
meta.summary: Trader, with T-0003: "Found a key level Support/Resistance waiting for price to react multiple times to confirm its valid so either i would take long for reclaim-retest-accept or short in case of losing the level again, which it did." Demonstrated once, as a 1m scalp without top-down analysis.

1.0.source: Stated by the trader with T-0003 (SOLUSDT 1m scalp), 2026-09-26
1.0.direction: Both. Long on reclaim-retest-accept; short when the level is lost again (deviation) and retested.
1.0.level_definition: Key support/resistance level drawn from a wick. It is valid once price has reacted to it multiple times. T-0003: tapped, lost, reclaimed and lost again. The trader's chart note reads (translated from Greek): "Possible resistance point. For validity, ideally we see extra resistances/supports."
required_conditions: A key level validated by multiple reactions.
Long: the level is reclaimed, retested from above, and accepted.
Short: the level is lost again (the reclaim was a deviation), then retested from below.
confirmation: Retest of the level from the other side
confluences: Red line: key level drawn from a wick, tapped multiple times

entry_models.reclaim_retest_accept: Long: on the retest after the level is reclaimed and accepted.
entry_models.deviation_retest: Short: on the retest from below after the level is lost again (T-0003).

1.0.stop_model: Beyond the latest swing before price broke the level, in case it reclaims the level. For a short, the latest high before the break (T-0003: 85.7453, the 20:32 high before the 20:33 break).
1.0.leverage_model: Isolated margin, within the 50% margin-loss rule. Higher leverage when the invalidation % is small (T-0003: 0.24% stop, 20x).
1.0.context: The trader called T-0003 risky because no top-down analysis was done: only the 1m chart was used, so higher-timeframe levels that could invalidate the setup were not checked.

management.invalidation: Stop beyond the latest swing before the break (see stop_model).

do_not_trade_when: Best target gives less than 2.5R (the trader's general rule).
open_questions: 1. How many reactions make a level valid: two, three, more?
2. How is the target chosen? T-0003 exited at 84.9409 (2.94R).
3. For scalps, which higher timeframes does the top-down analysis use?
4. Fees: are they inside the 1% risk? With a 0.24% stop, trading fees are a large share of 1R (see T-0003).

5. T-0003 timing: price traded through the 84.9409 target at about 21:01-21:04, about 24 minutes after entry, but you report 45 minutes. Was the TP a resting order, or did you close by hand at about 21:25?

meta.name: Supply/Demand + Price Action / Market Structure (liquidity confluences)
meta.summary: Trader's main strategy, in their words: "supply/demand level and price action/market structure, adding few confluences with liquidity levels". The long-side sequence was demonstrated in T-0001. The trader confirmed that every rule mirrors for shorts from supply (2026-09-26).

1.0.source: Stated by the trader with T-0001 (AAVE 4H), 2026-09-26
required_conditions: Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high. A wick or move through it without a close does not count.
confluences: Potential resistance level (used for the target)
1.0.entry_model: Primary: long at the extreme demand level. Secondary (used in T-0001 when the primary was missed): long on the reclaim of the swept inducement level (former equal lows) as support.
1.0.target_model: Next resistance level. In T-0001: the wick + higher-low level (yellow line).

1.1.source: Trader's answers, 2026-09-26 (follow-up to T-0001). Clarifies v1.0; no rule changed (CHG-001).
market_structure: Lower low: a candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). A wick below without a close is not a lower low.
Higher high: a candle must CLOSE above the previous high (its wick). ('vice versa')
Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
required_conditions: Bullish CHoCH on the 4H, close-based (see market_structure).
confluences: Potential resistance level (used for the target)

zones.extreme_demand: "The red box." In T-0001 it spans about 85.61 to 88.05, which matches the wick-to-wick range (about 85.73 to 88.00) of the lowest candle at the lower low, within about 0.1. The exact construction rule is pending (open question 3).

entry_models.extreme_demand: Primary: long at the extreme demand level (the red box).
entry_models.reclaim: Secondary: long when price reclaims the swept inducement level (former equal lows) as support. Used when the primary entry was missed (T-0001).

1.1.stop_model: At the level where the setup is invalidated: a return there means the move was a deviation or fakeout. Trader's words: "invalidated setup - possible deviation/fakeout". The mechanical placement is pending (open question 1). T-0001: 87.59, inside the red box, about 1.2 above the sweep low (86.40).
1.1.target_model: Next resistance level. High R:R is sought: "Hunting good RR setups is important." T-0001: the yellow line, 4.57R planned. No minimum R:R stated (open question 5).
1.1.leverage_model: Chosen from the entry-to-stop distance. T-0001: stop 3.14% (trader's figure) -> 10x. Leverage does not change the 1% risk; it sets the margin posted and the liquidation distance. The mapping rule and margin mode are pending (open question 4).

management.invalidation: Stop at the invalidation level (see stop_model).

open_questions: 1. Stop placement, mechanically. T-0001's stop (87.59) sat inside the red box, about 1.2 above the sweep low (86.40). Is it below the reclaim candle, a fixed point inside the zone, below the sweep wick, or something else?

2. Which lows count for the close-below rule? Read literally, it turns 4H structure bearish before T-0001's entry: Apr 18-19 closes fell below the post-CHoCH swing lows (about 103.04 and 97.08), and the Apr 20 candle closed at about 87.12, below the equal lows. Is only the major low (the lower low at the red box, about 85.73) protected, with smaller lows treated as internal structure or inducement?
3. Red box construction: is it the full wick-to-wick range of the lowest candle at the lower low?
4. Leverage: what rule maps stop distance to leverage (3.14% -> 10x), and do you use isolated or cross margin?
5. Is there a minimum R:R below which you skip a setup?
6. Do all rules mirror for shorts (supply zones, bearish CHoCH by a close below the last higher low)?

1.2.source: Trader's answers, 2026-09-26, to the v1.1 open questions. Clarifies v1.1; no rule changed (CHG-002).
1.2.direction: Both. Longs from demand, shorts from supply. Every rule mirrors (trader: '6) yes').
market_structure: Lower low: a candle must CLOSE below the previous low (its wick). A wick below without a close is not a lower low.
Higher high: a candle must CLOSE above the previous high (its wick).
Bullish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE above the last lower high.
Bearish CHoCH: a candle CLOSE below the last higher low (mirror, confirmed).
required_conditions: CHoCH on the 4H in the trade's direction, close-based (see market_structure).
confirmation: Reversal on the 4H (bullish for longs, bearish for shorts)
Extreme demand level (longs) / extreme supply level (shorts)
confluences: Strong momentum + volume in the trade's direction
Inducement (equal lows below for longs, equal highs above for shorts)
Potential opposing level (used for the target)

zones.extreme_demand: The full wick-to-wick range of the candle at the lower low that formed massive volume and a point of interest (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: 85.61 to 88.05.
zones.extreme_supply: Mirror: the full wick-to-wick range of the high-volume candle at the higher high.

entry_models.extreme_demand: Primary (long): at the extreme demand level.
entry_models.extreme_supply: Primary (short): at the extreme supply level (mirror).
entry_models.reclaim: Secondary: longs when price reclaims a swept level as support; shorts when price loses a swept level and retests it as resistance. Used when the primary entry was missed (T-0001).

1.2.stop_model: Placed where the setup is invalidated. Longs: below the demand zone, the swing low, or a liquidity level. Shorts: above the supply zone, the swing high, or a liquidity level (trader, 2026-09-26). T-0001: at a liquidity level from the left that had been reclaimed as support. A return there means price reverses lower or goes into consolidation, and the setup is invalid.
1.2.target_model: Next opposing level. High R:R is hunted: 1:3 minimum preferred, 1:2.5 accepted (trader, 2026-09-26).
1.2.leverage_model: Isolated margin. Leverage is chosen so that the loss on the posted margin at the stop (stop distance % x leverage) does not exceed 50%: leverage <= 50 / stop %. T-0001: 3.14% x 10x = 31.4%. Leverage never changes the 1% risk.

management.invalidation: Stop at the invalidation level (see stop_model).

open_questions: 1. Which lows does the close-below rule apply to? After the AAVE CHoCH, candles closed below the Apr 15 swing low (about 97.08) and later below the equal lows (about 87.12 close on Apr 20). Was structure still bullish because only the lower low at the red box (about 85.73) mattered? Or did those closes turn it bearish?
2. When the zone edge, the swing low and a liquidity level are all possible stops, which one is chosen: the nearest that invalidates the setup, the one under the most liquidity, or another rule?
3. 'Massive volume': how much more than usual? For example, at least 2x the average of the previous 20 candles.
4. Target: when several opposing levels exist, is it the first one that gives at least 2.5R, or the strongest level?
5. Equal lows/highs: how close must they be to count as equal? In T-0001 they sat within about 0.4 (about 0.45% of price).

changes.statement: Trader, 2026-09-26: "Entry to SL range (invalidation) was 3,14% so I used 10x leverage. Risk management always goes to 1%. *IMPORTANT* Creating a Lower low must close BELOW the previous wick/low and vise versa. 1) invalidated setup - possible deviation/fakeout 2) 1% risk per trade 3) I barely use break even and partials, I hold until TP hits. Hunting good RR setups is important 4) red box 5) 4h"
changes.note: These rules were in force when T-0001 was taken; v1.0 recorded them incompletely. T-0001 and T-0002 are retagged to 1.1 so per-version statistics are not split by a documentation change.

changes.statement: Trader, 2026-09-26: "1) stop mostly gets placed to invalidate a setup ... I place my stop loss below demand/supply or swing low/high or below/above a liquidity level. 2) on AAVE chart, stop was the liquidity level which reclaimed support level from left ... in case price would reverse back there and prices moves lower or enters a consolidation phase. 3) its the full wick to wick range which formed a massive volume and point of interest. 4) ... leverage planning not to exceed -50% ('-31,4% was the example of AAVE stop') which means I use an isolated margin. 5) I prefer hunting 1:3RR minimum, however I could enter a trade with 1:2,5RR as well. 6) yes [rules mirror for shorts]"
changes.note: Rules in force when T-0001 was taken. T-0001 and T-0002 retagged to 1.2.

journal.before:
Reconstructed from the trader's account on 2026-09-26 (after the outcome, so not hindsight-proof).
Bias bearish, 1m execution. Key level: red line drawn from a wick. Price tapped it multiple
times, reclaimed it and lost it again. Plan: short the deviation on the retest of the level.
Stop: the latest high before price broke below the level, in case it reclaims the level. Leverage 20x
because the invalidation % was low. Risk 1%.
journal.after:
Closed in profit at 2.94R. Trader: "It was a risky trade however because there wasn't any Top Down
Analysis while I was focused only at a LTF chart so the setup would get invalidated."
Key point (trader): find a key S/R level, wait for price to react multiple times to confirm it is
valid, then long on reclaim-retest-accept or short if the level is lost again, which it was.

observed: BTCC SOL/USDT perpetual, 1m, Apr 19 2026, UTC+3. Position tool: entry 85.5412, stop 85.7453, target 84.9409.
Prices marked 'about' were read from chart pixels, calibrated on 18 axis ticks (max residual 0.0034, about 1.5 px).
The red line (about 85.543) starts at the 18:36 wick low (about 85.547).
20:04-20:09: closes below the level (low about 85.31). 20:12: close back above (about 85.61).
20:22: high about 85.95. 20:27: pullback low about 85.567 held above the level.
20:32: high about 85.740, the latest high before the break (the stop is 85.7453). 20:33: close below the level (about 85.47).
20:40: retest from below, high about 85.558, which fills the 85.5412 short. After entry the highest price was that same candle; the stop was never approached.
The target was traded through at about 21:01-21:07 (lows about 84.94, 84.916, 84.925, 84.923), about 21-27 minutes after entry. The 21:24 candle closed at about 84.941.
Chart note (Greek, translated): 'Possible resistance point. For validity, ideally we see extra resistances/supports.'
RSI pane (with its moving average) read about 40-45 near entry. The trader did not use it.
interpreted: The chart matches the trader's account: level from a wick, lost, reclaimed, lost again, retested from below, short.
The 1m structure was bearish (lower highs from about 86.9 to about 85.74), which supports the short bias on this timeframe alone.
Risk decomposition (tj size, fees excluded): stop 0.239%, effective leverage 4.19x, margin 4.8% lost at the stop at 20x, max 209.6x under the 50% rule, isolated liquidation about 89.37.

The 45-minute duration conflicts with the chart: a resting TP at 84.9409 would have filled at about 21:01-21:04. Either the TP was not resting or the exit was manual at about 21:25. R is the same either way.
hypotheses: Fees may matter most on tight-stop scalps. HYPOTHETICAL fees (BTCC's actual fees unknown), via tj: 0.02%/side turns 2.94R gross into 2.38R net; 0.05%/side turns it into 1.78R and fees are 30% of 1R. Both fall below the 2.5R minimum. Sizing 1% on price distance alone would really risk 1.17% or 1.42% of equity.
Trades with top-down analysis may perform differently from LTF-only trades. Compare with ./tj compare top_down yes no once there is enough data.

review.lesson: A clean LTF execution of the key-level deviation-retest, taken without top-down analysis, so the context dimension is empty. The outcome was good; the process was mixed. Do not let the win reinforce skipping the higher timeframes.
review.actionable_change: Process: run the top-down analysis before LTF entries; record the timeframe chain on every trade.

observed: BloFin AAVE/USDT perpetual, 4H. Position tool: entry 90.41, stop 87.59, target 103.30 (labelled).
(103.30 - 90.41) / (90.41 - 87.59) = 4.57 via tj: matches the trader's stated R:R.
Lower low about 85.7 on Apr 7-8, the base of the red box (about 85.6 to 88.05).
Reversal on Apr 8 stayed below the green CH line (about 97.9); no close above it until Apr 13-14.
Equal lows around 89.0 to 89.4 on Apr 9-13 (red line 89.36). One wick about 88.75 near Apr 13 dipped below the line before the CHoCH.
Apr 14 candles: bodies topped about 103.2, wick about 104.05. Apr 17 lower wick about 103.0. The yellow line (about 103.3) sits across both.
Rally to above 115 on Apr 16-17, then full retrace on Apr 18-20. The sweep wick low was about 86.40, inside the red box and above the Apr 7-8 lower low.
The Apr 20 bullish reversal candle opened about 87.1 and closed about 89.9, back above 89.36. The entry at 90.41 came on the following candle.
After entry: low about 89.9 (Apr 22 wick), then about 91.0 in early May. The stop at 87.59 was not approached.
Highest price before TP was about 100.71 on Apr 27 (3.65R at the planned stop). Price then fell back to about 91.0 before the May 10 rally to the 103.30 target.
No volume pane on the chart. The volume confluence cannot be verified from this image.
Prices marked 'about' were read from chart pixels, calibrated on the labelled levels, to within about 0.1.
interpreted: The sequence is lower low, failed CHoCH, equal-low inducement, CHoCH by close, then a pullback that swept the inducement into extreme demand. The chart matches the trader's account.
The yellow line is a flip level: the Apr 14 breakout highs, then retested as support by the Apr 17 wick (the trader's 'wick + higher low'). The trader used it later as resistance and TP.
The stop at 87.59 sits inside the extreme demand zone, about 1.2 above the sweep low (86.40) and about 1.9 above the protected lower low (85.7). It is tighter than the structural invalidation.
hypotheses: A reclaim of the swept inducement level may be a valid secondary entry when the primary extreme-demand entry is missed (n=1).
Stops inside the demand zone above the sweep low may raise nominal R:R at the cost of more stop-outs on zone retests (untested, n=1).

outside_control: Not available when price reached the extreme demand zone (primary entry missed, T-0002)
20-day chop between about 90 and 101 before the target
review.lesson: When the primary entry at extreme demand was missed, a reclaim of the swept inducement level gave a defined-risk re-entry that captured the move. This is one example: track reclaim entries and extreme-demand entries separately. The stop sat at a liquidity level from the left that had been reclaimed as support. A return there would have invalidated the reclaim (reversal lower or consolidation), so the stop protects the reclaim thesis, not the whole demand zone.
review.actionable_change: Process only: define which stop candidate the bot picks when several exist (strategy v1.2, open question 2).

definitions.label: Top-down
definitions.rule: HTF context, key levels, then LTF execution (timeframes.top_down)

definitions.label: Valid setup
definitions.rule: Setup valid under the strategy version (review.setup_validity)

definitions.label: Leverage
definitions.rule: Stop % x leverage at most 50% of margin

definitions.label: Stop
definitions.rule: Stop respected: not moved, widened or removed

stages.name: 1. Specify the rules
stages.goal: Every rule becomes mechanical: a program reading it takes the same trades you do. Losses and shorts are required because a rulebook learned only from winning longs has never seen its failure modes.

stages.name: 2. Codify and verify the detector
stages.goal: Code that scans 4H OHLCV + volume finds the setups you journaled, with the same zone, stop and target. If the code disagrees with you, a backtest would test a different strategy.

criteria.label: Detector reproduces journaled setups
criteria.target: At least 80% of journaled setups found with matching zone, stop and target; every miss explained

stages.name: 3. Backtest out of sample
stages.goal: Hundreds of historical setups are replayed with fees, slippage and funding. This is where the sample size comes from: manual trading cannot produce it fast enough.

criteria.label: Out-of-sample expectancy is positive
criteria.target: 95% CI lower bound of expectancy > 0 on held-out data; n from the sample-size table, never below 100

criteria.label: Result holds across conditions
criteria.target: At least 2 trend regimes and 3 assets; no single asset or month carries the result

criteria.label: Drawdown is survivable at 1% risk
criteria.target: Worst simulated drawdown and losing streak accepted by the trader before going live

stages.name: 4. Forward test without money
stages.goal: The bot runs live on the exchange's data and logs orders without sending them.

criteria.label: Forward signals match the backtest
criteria.target: At least 30 signals; expectancy inside the backtest's confidence interval; zero execution errors

stages.name: 5. Live at reduced risk
stages.goal: Real orders at a quarter of the normal risk, with every safety control switched on.

criteria.label: Safety controls verified
criteria.target: All items in `safety` below are in place and tested

criteria.label: Live results match the backtest
criteria.target: At least 30 live trades at 0.25% risk; results inside the backtest's confidence interval

stages.name: 6. Full risk
stages.goal: Scale to the normal 1% risk only after live evidence agrees with the backtest.

criteria.label: Scaled to 1% risk
criteria.target: Trader's explicit decision, recorded with the live report as evidence

sample_size.note: Trades needed so that, if the edge is real, the 95% confidence interval of expectancy excludes zero 80% of the time. Two-outcome model (every loss -1R), so real needs are somewhat higher.

safety: API keys never go into chat, the repository or kb.json. They live only in the bot server's secret store or environment.
Keys have trade permission only: withdrawals disabled, IP-whitelisted to the bot's server.
The bot trades a dedicated sub-account funded with only the capital it may risk.
Every order is placed with its exchange-side stop, sized by the 1% rule, with leverage capped by the 50% margin-loss rule.
Kill switches halt trading after a daily loss limit or a run of consecutive losses, and alert the trader.
Execution is deterministic code, not a language model: the same market data always produces the same orders, and every decision is logged.
